sentences.text: This genus contains only a single known species, Barrosasuchus neuquenianus.
Its upper jaw held up to thirteen teeth on each side, while the front of the snout carried four additional teeth.
A distinct opening located at the center of the lower jawline serves an unknown purpose but acts as a unique trait for this animal.
Three shapes of bony plates were preserved, mostly scattered on the belly, though a rear section formed a connected shield.
The specimen was found in February 2001 during an expedition near Plaza Huincul in Neuquén province.
The name combines the local mountain range with a Greek term for crocodile and references the region where the fossil was unearthed.
Researchers Coria and colleagues formally named this genus in 2018, establishing the species as the basis for the group.
Taxonomically, it belongs to the family Peirosauridae within the broader group of notosuchian crocodile relatives.
It is classified within the class Reptilia.
This reptile inhabited Patagonia during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, roughly between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago.
